node.app-source.title: App sound

node.mic-input.title: Microphone
node.sound-button.title: Sound button
node.sound-button.desc: Plays a sound when pressed. Press again to pause, once more to continue.
node.volume.title: Volume
node.volume.desc: Makes the sound quieter or louder.
node.speaker-out.title: Headphones
node.virtual-out.title: Virtual microphone
node.virtual-out.desc: The sound goes to the virtual cable. In Discord or OBS, pick its microphone.
panel.empty: Select a node or a wire to see its settings.
panel.hint: To connect nodes, drag a wire from the circle on the right to the circle on the left.
notice.recovered: The project file was damaged. A copy was saved as {file}; a new project is open.

notice.cycle: Cannot connect like this: the sound would go in a circle.

map.nodeDesc: Map node. Drag with the mouse to move it.
hotkeys.title: Hotkeys
hotkeys.hint: They work only while the SoundBimba window is active and not while you type in a text field. They do not interfere with games.
hotkeys.displaced: This combination belonged to “{action}” — it is now turned off there.
param.appsEmpty: No program is playing sound right now
param.noCableHint: Virtual cable not found. Install VB-CABLE from vb-audio.com/Cable and restart the computer.
panel.soundOffHint: Sound is off now. Turn it on with the “Sound off” button at the top left.
notice.latencyMeasuring: Checking latency through the virtual cable… About two seconds.
notice.latency: Latency SoundBimba → virtual microphone: ≈ {output} ms. Including sound capture ≈ {total} ms.
error.latency: Could not measure latency: the test signal did not reach the virtual microphone.
error.latencyNoCable: Could not measure latency: virtual cable not found.
param.fileFormats: WAV, MP3, OGG and FLAC of any length.
param.label: Button name
buttons.title: SoundBimba buttons
buttons.none: No buttons yet. Add a “Sound button” node on the map.
buttons.soundOff: Sound is off — buttons do not play. Turn it on in the main window.
simple.noVolume: No volume controls yet. In the workspace, put a “Volume” node between a source and an output — it will appear here.
button.seekHint: Click the ring to jump: the top is the start, clockwise towards the end.
templates.title: Ready-made setups
templates.hint: The setup is added to the map below what is already there. Nothing is erased. Then pick apps, devices and sounds in the nodes.
template.soundpad-discord.title: Sound buttons in Discord
template.soundpad-discord.desc: Your voice and button sounds go to the virtual microphone; you also hear the sounds in your headphones.
template.game-to-mic.title: Game sound into the mic
template.game-to-mic.desc: Friends hear you and the chosen app (game, player) through the virtual microphone.
template.music-to-stream.title: Quiet music for a stream
template.music-to-stream.desc: Music from a player plays quietly in the background, your voice on top. Pick the virtual microphone in OBS.
template.hear-myself.title: Hear yourself
template.hear-myself.desc: Your microphone in your headphones — handy to check how you sound.
notice.templateAdded: Setup “{name}” added. Pick apps, devices and sounds in its nodes.
cable.title: Virtual cable
cable.whatFor: To send sound from SoundBimba into Discord, OBS or a game as a microphone, you need the free VB-CABLE virtual cable. SoundBimba does not install it — you do it yourself, once.
cable.notFound: Cable not found. Install it with the steps below.
cable.step1: Open the official website in your browser:
cable.step2: Download the VB-CABLE archive for Windows and unpack it to any folder.
cable.step4: Click “Install Driver” and wait until it finishes.
cable.step5: Restart the computer and click “Check again”.
cable.testing: Sending a quiet test signal through the cable… About two seconds.
cable.works: The link works. Latency ≈ {output} ms, ≈ {total} ms including sound capture.
cable.failed: The test signal did not arrive. Check that “CABLE Output” is not disabled in Windows sound settings and try again.
cable.tip: In Discord, OBS or a game choose the “CABLE Output” microphone. In SoundBimba — the “Virtual microphone” node.
welcome.title: Hi! This is SoundBimba
welcome.text: Here you build sound like a diagram: sources on the left (apps, microphone, sound buttons), outputs on the right (headphones, virtual microphone), wires in between. Where shall we start?
empty.title: The map is empty
empty.hint: Take a ready-made setup, or add nodes with “Add node” and connect them with wires — from the dot on a node’s right to the dot on another’s left.
clear.title: Clear everything?
clear.text: All nodes and wires will be removed from the map. This cannot be undone. If you may need the setup later, save it first with “Project → Export”.
templates.mineEmpty: Nothing here yet. Save the current map as a template or open a template file (.bmb).
templates.saveCurrentEmpty: The map is empty — nothing to save.
templates.name: Name
templates.deleteConfirm: Delete the template “{name}”? This cannot be undone.
reason.not-template: this is not a SoundBimba template
reason.newer-template: the template was made by a newer SoundBimba
templates.deleteBuiltinConfirm: Remove “{name}” from the list? You can bring it back with “Restore deleted”.
node.compressor.title: Compressor
node.compressor.desc: Evens out loudness: makes loud parts quieter, then raises everything. Your voice sounds steadier and louder, without overload.
preset.louder.hint: Lifts quiet speech a lot, keeps loud parts from overloading
preset.strong.hint: Dense even sound, like on the radio
param.thresholdHint: From what loudness to start compressing. The lower, the more often it works.
param.ratioHint: How many times to squeeze what is above the threshold. 1:1 — no compression.
param.makeupHint: How much to raise the whole sound after compression.
param.attackHint: How fast to start compressing when it gets loud.
param.releaseHint: How fast to let go when it gets quieter.
node.voice-morpher.title: Voice morpher
node.voice-morpher.desc: Changes your voice: lower or higher, wobble, robot, radio, echo. Put it between the microphone and the virtual microphone.
voice.radio.hint: Narrow sound, like a walkie-talkie or phone
voice.alien.hint: Alien: a bit higher, the voice “floats”, a light spaceship echo
param.pitchHint: Lower or higher, in semitones. 12 is one octave.
param.pitchDelay: While the pitch is changed or wobbling, the voice is delayed by about 20 ms — that is how pitch shifting works.
simple.morpherNone: No morpher yet. Take the “Changed voice” template (“Project → Templates…”) or put a “Voice morpher” node between the microphone and an output on the map.
template.voice-changer.title: Changed voice
template.voice-changer.desc: Your voice goes through the morpher into the virtual microphone — in Discord you will sound like a robot, monster or chipmunk.
node.denoise.title: Noise suppression
node.denoise.desc: Keeps your voice and removes background: fans, hum, keyboard. Put it right after the microphone.
param.denoiseHint: Runs the RNNoise neural network right on your computer, offline. Adds about 20 ms of delay to your voice. A flat “shhh” hiss is reduced only a little — it sounds like speech.
template.clean-voice.title: Clean voice
template.clean-voice.desc: Noise suppression removes the background, the compressor makes your voice even and louder — then it goes to the virtual microphone.
original.normalHint: The app plays where it always did; SoundBimba takes a copy.
original.deviceHint: The app itself will play on the chosen device (e.g. only these headphones). The copy in SoundBimba stays.
original.onlyHint: The original goes to a device you don’t listen to (e.g. monitor audio) — you hear the app only the way it passes through your map.
original.onlyDefaultWarning: You probably listen to this device — choose one you can’t hear (e.g. monitor audio).
original.applied: Changed in Windows settings: {exe} plays on “{device}”. If the sound didn’t move, restart the app or its playback. SoundBimba restores it when you choose “As usual”, delete the node, turn sound off or close SoundBimba.
original.waiting: Will apply when {exe} starts playing sound (Windows only changes this for an app that is playing).
original.error: Windows did not accept the setting. Details are in “Save diagnostics”.
original.soundOff: SoundBimba sound is off now — the Windows setting is restored.

templates.updateConfirm: Replace the scheme in “{name}” with the one on the map now?
error.templateUpdate: Could not save changes to the template: {reason}
node.chip.title: Chip
node.chip.desc: A whole scheme in one block. Double-click to open it and build the scheme inside. The "Chip input" and "Chip output" nodes inside become its pins outside.
node.chip-in.title: Chip input
node.chip-in.desc: A pin on the left of the chip: the sound fed into it from outside comes out here.
node.chip-out.title: Chip output
node.chip-out.desc: A pin on the right of the chip: whatever comes here leaves the chip.
reason.bad-port: a wire goes to a chip pin that does not exist
reason.too-deep: too many chips inside each other
